items.headline: Mid-year reinsurance renewals settle softer, easing the capital backdrop for privately-underwritten workers-comp markets
items.summary: Brokers reported that the 1 July 2026 reinsurance renewals completed against record global capacity, with loss-free Australia and New Zealand programs pricing down roughly 10–15% and cedants buying more vertical limit, while casualty lines held broadly stable rather than softening. The driver is sustained reinsurer profitability and an increasingly competitive, buyer-friendly market rather than any workers-comp-specific event.
items.so_what: Cheaper, more abundant reinsurance is a modest tailwind for the capital and pricing position of the privately-underwritten workers-comp schemes (WA, TAS, NT, ACT) and the licensed insurers that operate across them, and a favourable backdrop for APRA-regulated capital generally; for the NSW Nominal Insurer — which is statutory and self-funded through premiums rather than reinsurance-dependent — the read-across is indirect, so this is situational awareness only. Worth noting that a soft reinsurance market can persist only until a large loss event turns it.
